title: 江南春
author: 杜牧
intro: Four lines paint the whole Yangtze delta in spring: birdsong, green and red, wine flags in the wind — and then hundreds of old temples fading into the misty rain. A postcard that quietly turns into a reflection on history.
analysis: 这首诗写江南的春天，像一幅很大的风景画。第一句从“千里”写起，黄莺在叫，绿树映着红花，有声音也有颜色。第二句写水边的村子、靠山的城墙和迎风飘动的酒旗，充满生活气息。后两句从眼前转向历史：南朝（公元420—589年）的皇帝信佛，在这一带建了几百座寺庙，“四百八十”是说很多，不是准确数字。如今这些楼台都隐在蒙蒙的烟雨之中。前两句明亮热闹，后两句朦胧安静，一明一暗形成对比。诗人没有直接评论，却让人想到：当年花大力气建寺求佛的王朝，最后都消失了。所以这首诗既是写景名作，也有怀古的味道。
analysisEn: This poem is a wide landscape painting of spring in Jiangnan, the land south of the lower Yangtze. The first line covers “a thousand li” at once: orioles singing, green leaves setting off red flowers — sound and colour together. The second line zooms in on villages by the water, town walls against the hills, and wine-shop flags flapping in the breeze, full of everyday life. Then the poem turns from the present to history. The emperors of the Southern Dynasties (420–589) were devout Buddhists and built hundreds of temples in this region; “four hundred and eighty” simply means “a great many”. Now all those towers and terraces stand half-hidden in the misty rain. The first half is bright and lively, the second soft and hazy, and the contrast does the talking. Du Mu makes no comment, but readers are left to think: the dynasties that spent so much on temples are long gone. That is why the poem is loved both as scenery and as a quiet meditation on the past.
background: Du Mu (803–c. 852), grandson of a famous chancellor, was a Tang official and one of the finest writers of the short quatrain. He spent several years in the Jiangnan region as a young official, and this poem is traditionally read as a reflection on the late Tang court’s lavish support of Buddhism.
pronunciation: 多少 duō shǎo（不读 duō shao）。“四百八十寺”的“十”按今音读 shí。
version: 采用通行教材版本。明代杨慎认为“千里”应作“十里”（千里之内的莺啼谁也听不到），清人何文焕等反驳说这是诗的夸张写法，通行本都作“千里”。

lines.py: qiān lǐ yīng tí lǜ yìng hóng
lines.lit: For a thousand li orioles sing, green sets off red;
lines.en: For a thousand miles the orioles sing, green leaves against red blossoms;

lines.py: shuǐ cūn shān guō jiǔ qí fēng
lines.lit: water villages, hill-town walls, wine flags in the wind.
lines.en: villages by the water, walls against the hills, wine flags stirring in the breeze.

lines.py: nán cháo sì bǎi bā shí sì
lines.lit: The Southern Dynasties’ four hundred and eighty temples —
lines.en: Of all the temples the Southern Dynasties built,

lines.py: duō shǎo lóu tái yān yǔ zhōng
lines.lit: how many towers and terraces in the mist and rain.
lines.en: how many towers still stand, dim in the misty rain.

words.note: 莺：黄莺；啼：鸟叫。现代汉语说“鸟叫”。
现代汉语“反映”“映衬”的“映”。
古义，今天很少单用，“城郭”还在书面语里出现。
古代酒店门口挂的布招牌，今天叫“招牌”。
宋、齐、梁、陈四个朝代，都城在今天的南京。
现代汉语仍用，如“寺庙”“少林寺”。
“烟”在这里指雾气，不是抽烟的烟。现代汉语有“烟雨江南”的说法。
这里是感叹“有多少”，现代汉语多用来提问。

imagery.name: 鸟
imagery.zh: “莺啼”是黄莺在叫，一开头就用声音把春天带进来。
imagery.en: The orioles’ singing opens the poem with sound: spring arrives through the ears first.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: “酒旗”是酒家门口挂的旗子，在风里飘动，写出江南村镇的热闹和生活气。
imagery.en: The wine-shop flags flapping in the wind show busy, lived-in riverside villages.

imagery.name: 楼
imagery.zh: “楼台”指南朝留下的寺院建筑，曾经的辉煌如今只剩下烟雨里的影子。
imagery.en: The towers and terraces are the old Southern Dynasties temples — past glory now half-hidden in the rain.

imagery.name: 雨
imagery.zh: “烟雨”是江南特有的蒙蒙细雨，让画面变得朦胧，也带出一点怀古的伤感。
imagery.en: The misty drizzle typical of the south blurs the scene and adds a soft sadness about the past.
